text:
maya: Heads-up — after the coalescer rollout yesterday I'm seeing p99 climb ~120ms on the short-sequence traffic and a big drop in our prompt-prefill cache hit-rate. Digging in now, but wanted to surface here.

ben_chang: ack. do you have numbers? is this only canary or prod too?

maya: canary only so far. hit-rate on prompt prefill went from ~82% -> ~41% over the 30m window after deploy. baseline already had continuous batching enabled.

leila: interesting. could be that coalescer is changing batch composition and mixing prefixes, which reduces effective cache reuse. any profiling traces?

maya: pasted an excerpt from the perf run:
```
2026-03-17T18:12:03Z request_id=abc token_count=16 kernel=matmul_generic seq=22 cache_lookup=miss
2026-03-17T18:12:03Z request_id=def token_count=8 kernel=fused_attn seq=12 cache_lookup=miss
2026-03-17T18:12:03Z request_id=ghi token_count=32 kernel=matmul_generic seq=40 cache_lookup=hit
```
Looks like kernel selection switched to matmul_generic for a lot of short examples — that wasn’t the case before.

ben_chang: hmm. switching kernels can change the way keys are canonicalized for KV indexing if we reorder tensors or pad differently. Did the coalescer change padding/order? @leila

leila: coalescer-v2 does opportunistic slice-merge across requests. It normalizes sequence lengths to the max in the micro-batch, and that can change the prefix fingerprint if our cache key included padded length/stride info.

sre_april: is the cache key currently: `model|version|prefill_hash|seq_len|kernel_tag`? if kernel_tag or seq_len get mutated by coalescing then keys diverge.

maya: yes, current key: `join(':', [model, ver, prefix_sha256, seq_len, kernel_shim])`. It was fine pre-rollout because kernel_shim was stable.

ben_chang: quick mitigation: drop kernel_shim from the cache key so cache matches purely on logical prefix content. risk: different kernel runtimes may produce slight numerics but for prefill (exact-match prefix) we should be safe.

leila: agreed but we need a controlled rollout. alternative: compute prefix-only key and attach a secondary tag for observability instead of keying on it.

maya: ran a quick sim locally — removing kernel_shim bumps hit-rate back to ~78% in the harness. but it also exposes a case where kernel-specific warmup paths expect different KV layout.

deploy-bot: Deployment started: coalescer-v2 -> canary (pods: 3)

infra-bot: Created PERF-4823: "coalescer-v2 reduces prefill cache hit-rate via kernel/pad keying" — assigned to eng-runtime

sre_april: short-term: roll back coalescer-v2 or set coalescer to preserve original per-request seq_len and kernel markers for prefill traffic. which is faster?

maya: rolling back canary now to v1 and will re-run the trace and bench. if rollback is slow we can flip a feature-flag to force legacy keying.

ben_chang: for longer term: update keying to use canonical prefix digest (content-only) + an independent perf label for kernel. and add a unit test verifying continuous batching preserves prefix digest across coalescing strategies.

leila: also add a small invariant check in the runtime: after any coalescing transform, assert that prefix_digest(request) == prefix_digest(post-transform) for requests that only differ by padding.

maya: plan: rollback canary -> run bench + diff profiles -> implement kernel_shim removal behind flag -> stage rollout. I'll post numbers here when done. thanks :heart:

ben_chang: thanks maya. if you need help with the bench harness or a quick patch ping me.

maya: will do. filing short writeup after the rollback. "
